⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Ajlah ibn Abd Allah al-Kindi, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Do not wear your garments in disobedience. Have you not heard the saying of Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi:"

"By the praise of God, I have never worn the garment of a wicked man,
nor have I covered myself with treachery."

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah related to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ata' informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas say regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾: "From sin." Then he said: "Pure garments" (naqiyy al-thiyab) is an expression in the language of the Arabs.

⁕ Sa'id ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Qadi narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: In the language of the Arabs: "pure garments."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From sins."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From sins."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: It is a phrase of the Arabic language which the Arabs used to say: "Purify your garments," that is, from sins.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: It means: purify them from disobedience. The Arabs used to call a man who broke his covenant and did not fulfil his promise "one whose garments are soiled," and when he fulfilled and reformed, they said: "one whose garments are pure."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From wickedness."

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From wickedness."

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾: "Do not wear your garments in disobedience."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From wickedness."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "From wickedness."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Ajlah, who heard Ikrimah say: "Do not wear your garments in disobedience."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Amir and Ata', who both said: "From faults."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Do not wear garments acquired through illegitimate earnings.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Let not your garments, which you wear, be from unlawful earnings." It is also said: "Do not wear your garments in disobedience."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Set right your deeds.

Those who said this:

⁕ Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i related to me, saying: Fudayl ibn Iyad narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Your deeds, set them right."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Your deeds, set them right. When a man's deeds were corrupt, they would say: 'So-and-so has soiled garments,' and when his deeds were good they would say: 'So-and-so has pure garments.'"

Others said concerning this what follows:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "You are neither a soothsayer nor a magician, so turn away from what they say."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Wash them with water and purify them of impurity.

Those who said this:

⁕ Abbas ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Musa ibn Abi Maryam, the owner of the pearls, who said: Ibn Awn informed us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Wash them with water."

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾: "The polytheists did not purify themselves, so He commanded him to purify himself and purify his garments."

This statement of Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd on this matter is the most apparent of its meanings. What Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ibn Zakariyya said is the view on which most of the early scholars (al-salaf) agree, that what is meant is: purify your body from sins. And God knows best what He intends by it.

﴿And shun the abomination!﴾

The readers (qurra') differed in reciting this. Some of the readers of Medina and most of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿al-rijza﴾ with a kasrah on the ra' (الرِّجْزَ), while some of the Meccan and Medinan readers recited ﴿al-rujza﴾ with a dammah on the ra' (الرُّجْزَ). Whoever recited with a dammah directed it toward the idols, and said: The meaning of the speech is: "and the idols, shun their worship and abandon serving them." Whoever recited with a kasrah directed it toward the punishment, and said: Its meaning is: "and the punishment, shun," that is, shun the deeds that brought punishment upon you.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations, and whichever one the reciter uses is correct. The dammah and the kasrah are two dialects with one meaning. We have not found any of the earlier people of interpretation who distinguished between their meanings, except, as has reached us, al-Kisa'i.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of al-rujz (الرُّجْزُ) in this place. Some of them said: It is the idols.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "That is, the wrath, which is the idols."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "The idols."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il (Abu Ja'far said: I think it is from me), from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "The idols."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾: Isaf and Na'ilah, two idols that were beside the House; whoever came to them would rub their faces, so God commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to avoid them and keep away from them.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "They are the idols."

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "The abomination is their gods which they worshipped. He commanded him to abandon them, so that he would not go to them or approach them."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: And sin and wickedness, shun.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "Wickedness."

*A tradition was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿And abandon the filth﴾: he said, "Abandon sin." We have already explained the meaning of al-rijz (filth) earlier, with its evidences, which make repeating them here unnecessary.*

* *

And His words: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) differed over its interpretation. Some of them said: the meaning is: "Do not give a gift, O Muhammad, in order to receive more than it."

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give a gift seeking to receive something better than it."
* Abu Humayd al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Abu Hayawa Shurayh ibn Yazid al-Hadrami narrated to me, saying: Artat narrated to me, on the authority of Damra ibn Habib and Abu al-Ahwas, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, they said: "Do not give anything in order that you may be given more than it."
* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Raja', on the authority of 'Ikrima, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give anything in order that you may be given more than it."
* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, saying: someone who heard 'Ikrima say informed me: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give a gift in order that you want to take more than it."
* Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Fudayl narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give in order that you may increase."
* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give anything in order that you may take more than it."
* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Salama, on the authority of al-Dahhak: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give in order that you may be given more than it."
* He said: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give in order that you may be given more than it."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give anything in order that you may increase."
* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Rawwad, on the authority of al-Dahhak, who said: "It is the lawful usury (al-riba al-halal), which was permitted to the Prophet ﷺ specifically."
* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hujayra, on the authority of al-Dahhak: "There are two kinds of riba: lawful and unlawful. The lawful is gifts, and the unlawful is usury."
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give anything; your only reward is the reciprocation and return of this world."
* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding (And do not give in order to receive more), he said: "Do not give anything in order that you may be rewarded with something better than it." Tawus also said this.
* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "You give wealth as a favour, hoping for something better than it, the reward in this world."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: "Do not give in order that you may be given more than it."
* He said: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give in order that you may increase."
* He said: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "It is specific to the Prophet ﷺ, and general for people, who are granted latitude."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: "Do not show favour to your Lord in order to regard your deeds as great."

Those who said this:

* Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Husayn narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not bestow your deed, regarding it as great, upon your Lord."
* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not bestow, regarding your deed as great."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Nafi' Abu Ghanim narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Sahl Kathir ibn Ziyad, on the authority of al-Hasan: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not bestow, regarding your righteous deed as great."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ja'far, on the authority of al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not let your deed seem great in your eyes, for what Allah has bestowed on you and given you is little."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: "Do not be weak in seeking to increase in good." They interpreted His words ﴿And do not give﴾ as meaning "do not be weak," from the saying "a rope that is mannin," meaning weak.

Those who said this:

* Abu Humayd ibn al-Mughira al-Himsi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salama narrated to us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not be weak in seeking to increase in good." He said: "Tamannun in the speech of the Arabs means 'to be weak.'"

Others said regarding this: "Do not bestow prophethood upon people, taking a reward from them for it."

Those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾: "Do not bestow prophethood and the Qur'an, with which We sent you, upon them, seeking from them in return something of the world."

The view that I hold to be most correct in this matter is the view of those who said: the meaning is: "And do not show favour to your Lord by regarding your righteous deed as great."

I say this is more correct because it occurs in the context of verses in which Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to strive in calling to Him and to be patient over the harm he suffers in doing so. Thus this verse is more fitting to be one of the kinds of those (commands) than to be of something else. It is reported on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud that in his recitation it was (wa la tamnun an tastakthir) [[Hadith 198. Badil, with a damma on the bā' and a fatḥa on the dāl: he is Ibn Maysara al-Uqayli, a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i). This report is connected by a sound chain, because 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq stated in it that "someone who heard the Prophet ﷺ" informed him, and the anonymity of a Companion does not harm, as is well known. Connecting the chain by mentioning an unnamed Companion is an addition from a trustworthy narrator, and so it is accepted.

Ibn Kathir (1: 54–55) mentioned this connected report, then pointed to the three mursal reports, then said: "In a report from 'Urwa there occurs the naming of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, and Allah knows best." However, he did not mention who transmitted the report from 'Urwa to which he refers. Then Ibn Kathir said: "Ibn Mardawayh has narrated, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, on the authority of Badil ibn Maysara, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: 'I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about "those who have earned anger," and he said: "The Jews." I said: "Those who have gone astray?" He said: "The Christians."' " The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in Fath al-Bari (8: 122) pointed to this report of Ibn Mardawayh from Abu Dharr "with a good chain." He also mentioned that the connected report of 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, "that someone who heard the Prophet ﷺ informed him," was narrated by Ahmad. These reports are also found in al-Suyuti (1: 16) and al-Shawkani (1: 14–15). The interpretation of (al-Dallin) will come with these chains at 210, 211, 212, 213. At 211 the identification of 'Urwa, who is in the chain at 197, will come.]]

* *

And His words: ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾.

He, may He be exalted, says: "And for your Lord, be patient over what you encounter of hardship in it."

A group of the interpreters said something similar to what we have said, though there is some difference among the interpreters on this.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾, he said: "Over what you were given."
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾, he said: "He bore a great task: fighting the Arabs, then the non-Arabs after the Arabs, for the sake of Allah."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: "And for your Lord, be patient over your giving."

Those who said this:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾, he said: "Be patient over your giving."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: "Be patient over your giving to Allah."
* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾, he said: "Your giving: be patient over it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 74, verses 1–7 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who are wrapped up (in your garments)! Arise and warn! And magnify your Lord! And purify your garments! And shun the abomination! And do not give, seeking to get more! And for your Lord, be patient!﴾

He, exalted is His praise, says: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, meaning: O you who wrap yourself in your garments when you sleep.

It is mentioned that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was addressed with this while he was wrapped in a qatifa (a thick woollen cloak).

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, he said: He was wrapped in a qatifa.

It is also mentioned that this verse was the first thing revealed of the Qur'an to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and that he was addressed with: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾.

As follows:

⁕ Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed us, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, while narrating about the interruption of revelation: "While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my head, and behold, the angel who had come to me at Hira was sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I was seized with terror from him, and I came to my family and said: 'Wrap me, wrap me!' So they wrapped me." Then God revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up! Arise and warn! And magnify your Lord! ...﴾ up to His words: ﴿And shun the abomination﴾. He said: Then the revelation followed in succession.

[Editorial note: Hadith no. 195. This chain is also sound. Mari ibn Qatari al-Kufi: Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (al-Thiqat), and al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (4/2/57), saying: "He heard Adi ibn Hatim; Simak ibn Harb narrated from him; he is counted among the Kufans." "Mari" is pronounced with a dammah on the m and a shaddah on the r with kasrah, and a shaddah on the y. "Qatari" has a fathah on the q and the t, and a shaddah on the y after the r. Part of it will also come later with the same chain, 209.

This hadith from Adi ibn Hatim is in origin a lengthy account of his conversion to Islam. Ahmad related it in full in al-Musnad (4:378–379), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, with the earlier chain (194). al-Tirmidhi (4:67) related it through Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Simak, from Abbad ibn Hubaysh, from Adi, and said: "This is a good, gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of Simak ibn Harb. Shu'bah narrated from Simak ibn Harb, from Abbad ibn Hubaysh, from Adi ibn Hatim, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the hadith in full." Part of it was narrated by al-Tayalisi in his Musnad (1040), from Amr ibn Thabit, "from one who heard Adi ibn Hatim." It has become clear to us from the narrations of al-Tabari here that Simak ibn Harb heard it from Abbad ibn Hubaysh and from Mari ibn Qatari, both from Adi, and that Simak ibn Harb did not transmit it alone, since Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated it from al-Sha'bi, from Adi. That al-Tirmidhi knew it only from the hadith of Simak does not preclude that others knew it through another route. Ibn Kathir mentioned it (1:54) from Ahmad's narration in al-Musnad, pointed to al-Tirmidhi's narration and to al-Tabari's narrations here, and then said: "This hadith of Adi has been related through several routes, and it has many wordings, too lengthy to mention." Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) mentioned it in al-Isabah, in Adi's biography (2:229), from the narrations of Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi. al-Suyuti mentioned from it (1:16) the explanation of the two words, and attributed it also to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih. Al-Shawkani did the same (1:15).]

Then Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir told me, saying: I asked Abu Salamah: "Which part of the Qur'an was revealed first?" He said: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾. I said: "They say ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾." Abu Salamah said: I asked Jabir ibn Abd Allah: "Which part of the Qur'an was revealed first?" He said: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾. I said: "They say: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾." He said: "I will not tell you except what the Prophet (ﷺ) told us, who said:"

⁕ The Prophet (ﷺ) related to us, saying: "I secluded myself at Hira'. When I had completed my seclusion, I descended, and I entered the valley, and I was called. I looked to my right and my left, behind me and in front of me, and I saw nothing. Then I looked above my head, and behold, he was sitting on a throne between the sky and the earth, so I feared him." This is what Uthman ibn Amr said; the actual wording is: "So I was seized with terror from him." "Then I met Khadijah and said: 'Wrap me, wrap me,' so they wrapped me, and poured water over me. Then God revealed to me: ﴿O you who are wrapped up! Arise and warn!﴾"

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Ali ibn Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: I asked Abu Salamah about the first part of the Qur'an to be revealed. He said: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ was revealed first. I said: "They say ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾." He said: I asked Jabir ibn Abd Allah, and he said: "I will not tell you except what..."

⁕ The Messenger of God (ﷺ) related to us, saying: "I secluded myself at Hira'. When I had completed my seclusion, I descended, and I heard a voice. I looked to my right and saw nothing, and I looked behind me and saw nothing. I raised my head and saw something. I came to Khadijah and said: 'Wrap me, and pour cold water over me.' Then ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ was revealed."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: The revelation was interrupted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for a period, and he grieved greatly, so he would run to the peaks of high mountains intending to throw himself down from them. Whenever he reached the summit of a mountain, Gabriel, peace be upon him, would appear to him and say: "You are the Prophet of God," and his anxiety would subside and his soul would be calmed. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to narrate about that. He said: "While I was walking one day, I saw the angel who used to come to me at Hira' on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was seized with terror from him, so I returned to Khadijah and said: 'Wrap me!' So they wrapped him, that is, covered him. Then God revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up! Arise and warn! And magnify your Lord! And purify your garments!﴾" Al-Zuhri said: The first thing revealed to him was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created...﴾ up to ﴿what he did not know﴾.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil, i.e., the early exegetes) differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾. Some of them said: The meaning is: O you who are wrapped in your garments.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, he said: O you who are sleeping.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, he said: The one wrapped in his garments.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: O you who are wrapped in prophethood and its burdens.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud was asked about this verse, ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, and he related to us from Ikrimah that he said: "You have wrapped yourself in this matter, so stand up for it."

* *

As for His words ﴿Arise and warn!﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Arise from your sleep and warn your people, who ascribe partners to God and worship other than Him, of God's punishment.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Arise and warn!﴾: that is, warn of God's punishment, His calamities among the nations, and the severity of His vengeance.

* *

As for His words ﴿And magnify your Lord!﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, glorify Him by worshipping Him, and direct your desires to Him in your needs, rather than any other deities or rivals.

* *

As for His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾:

The people of interpretation differed regarding its explanation. Some of them said: The meaning is: Do not wear your garments for disobedience, nor for treachery.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: Have you not heard the saying of Ghaylan ibn Salamah:

"By the praise of God, I have never worn the garment of a wicked man,
nor have I covered myself with treachery."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Musab ibn Salam narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man came to him while I was sitting, and said: "Tell me about the words of God: ﴿And purify your garments!﴾" He said: "Do not wear them for disobedience or for treachery." Then he said: "Have you not heard the saying of Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi:"

"By the praise of God, I have never worn the garment of a wicked man,
nor have I covered myself with treachery."

⁕ Sa'id ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Do not wear them for treachery, nor for wickedness," and then he quoted this poetry of Ghaylan ibn Salamah.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Ajlah ibn Abd Allah al-Kindi, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Do not wear your garments in disobedience. Have you not heard the saying of Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi:"

"By the praise of God, I have never worn the garment of a wicked man,
nor have I covered myself with treachery."

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah related to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ata' informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas say regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾: "From sin." Then he said: "Pure garments" (naqiyy al-thiyab) is an expression in the language of the Arabs.

⁕ Sa'id ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Qadi narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: In the language of the Arabs: "pure garments."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From sins."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From sins."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: It is a phrase of the Arabic language which the Arabs used to say: "Purify your garments," that is, from sins.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: It means: purify them from disobedience. The Arabs used to call a man who broke his covenant and did not fulfil his promise "one whose garments are soiled," and when he fulfilled and reformed, they said: "one whose garments are pure."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From wickedness."

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From wickedness."

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾: "Do not wear your garments in disobedience."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "From wickedness."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "From wickedness."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Ajlah, who heard Ikrimah say: "Do not wear your garments in disobedience."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Amir and Ata', who both said: "From faults."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Do not wear garments acquired through illegitimate earnings.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Let not your garments, which you wear, be from unlawful earnings." It is also said: "Do not wear your garments in disobedience."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Set right your deeds.

Those who said this:

⁕ Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i related to me, saying: Fudayl ibn Iyad narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Your deeds, set them right."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Your deeds, set them right. When a man's deeds were corrupt, they would say: 'So-and-so has soiled garments,' and when his deeds were good they would say: 'So-and-so has pure garments.'"

Others said concerning this what follows:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "You are neither a soothsayer nor a magician, so turn away from what they say."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Wash them with water and purify them of impurity.

Those who said this:

⁕ Abbas ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Musa ibn Abi Maryam, the owner of the pearls, who said: Ibn Awn informed us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, regarding ﴿And purify your garments!﴾, he said: "Wash them with water."

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And purify your garments!﴾: "The polytheists did not purify themselves, so He commanded him to purify himself and purify his garments."

This statement of Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd on this matter is the most apparent of its meanings. What Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ibn Zakariyya said is the view on which most of the early scholars (al-salaf) agree, that what is meant is: purify your body from sins. And God knows best what He intends by it.

﴿And shun the abomination!﴾

The readers (qurra') differed in reciting this. Some of the readers of Medina and most of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿al-rijza﴾ with a kasrah on the ra' (الرِّجْزَ), while some of the Meccan and Medinan readers recited ﴿al-rujza﴾ with a dammah on the ra' (الرُّجْزَ). Whoever recited with a dammah directed it toward the idols, and said: The meaning of the speech is: "and the idols, shun their worship and abandon serving them." Whoever recited with a kasrah directed it toward the punishment, and said: Its meaning is: "and the punishment, shun," that is, shun the deeds that brought punishment upon you.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations, and whichever one the reciter uses is correct. The dammah and the kasrah are two dialects with one meaning. We have not found any of the earlier people of interpretation who distinguished between their meanings, except, as has reached us, al-Kisa'i.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of al-rujz (الرُّجْزُ) in this place. Some of them said: It is the idols.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "That is, the wrath, which is the idols."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "The idols."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il (Abu Ja'far said: I think it is from me), from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "The idols."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾: Isaf and Na'ilah, two idols that were beside the House; whoever came to them would rub their faces, so God commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to avoid them and keep away from them.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "They are the idols."

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "The abomination is their gods which they worshipped. He commanded him to abandon them, so that he would not go to them or approach them."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: And sin and wickedness, shun.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And shun the abomination!﴾, he said: "Wickedness."

*A tradition was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿And abandon the filth﴾: he said, "Abandon sin." We have already explained the meaning of al-rijz (filth) earlier, with its evidences, which make repeating them here unnecessary.*

* *

And His words: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) differed over its interpretation. Some of them said: the meaning is: "Do not give a gift, O Muhammad, in order to receive more than it."

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give a gift seeking to receive something better than it."
* Abu Humayd al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Abu Hayawa Shurayh ibn Yazid al-Hadrami narrated to me, saying: Artat narrated to me, on the authority of Damra ibn Habib and Abu al-Ahwas, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, they said: "Do not give anything in order that you may be given more than it."
* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Raja', on the authority of 'Ikrima, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give anything in order that you may be given more than it."
* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, saying: someone who heard 'Ikrima say informed me: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give a gift in order that you want to take more than it."
* Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Fudayl narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give in order that you may increase."
* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give anything in order that you may take more than it."
* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Salama, on the authority of al-Dahhak: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give in order that you may be given more than it."
* He said: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give in order that you may be given more than it."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give anything in order that you may increase."
* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Rawwad, on the authority of al-Dahhak, who said: "It is the lawful usury (al-riba al-halal), which was permitted to the Prophet ﷺ specifically."
* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hujayra, on the authority of al-Dahhak: "There are two kinds of riba: lawful and unlawful. The lawful is gifts, and the unlawful is usury."
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give anything; your only reward is the reciprocation and return of this world."
* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding (And do not give in order to receive more), he said: "Do not give anything in order that you may be rewarded with something better than it." Tawus also said this.
* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "You give wealth as a favour, hoping for something better than it, the reward in this world."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: "Do not give in order that you may be given more than it."
* He said: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not give in order that you may increase."
* He said: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "It is specific to the Prophet ﷺ, and general for people, who are granted latitude."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: "Do not show favour to your Lord in order to regard your deeds as great."

Those who said this:

* Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Husayn narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not bestow your deed, regarding it as great, upon your Lord."
* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not bestow, regarding your deed as great."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Nafi' Abu Ghanim narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Sahl Kathir ibn Ziyad, on the authority of al-Hasan: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not bestow, regarding your righteous deed as great."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ja'far, on the authority of al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not let your deed seem great in your eyes, for what Allah has bestowed on you and given you is little."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: "Do not be weak in seeking to increase in good." They interpreted His words ﴿And do not give﴾ as meaning "do not be weak," from the saying "a rope that is mannin," meaning weak.

Those who said this:

* Abu Humayd ibn al-Mughira al-Himsi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salama narrated to us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾, he said: "Do not be weak in seeking to increase in good." He said: "Tamannun in the speech of the Arabs means 'to be weak.'"

Others said regarding this: "Do not bestow prophethood upon people, taking a reward from them for it."

Those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And do not give in order to receive more﴾: "Do not bestow prophethood and the Qur'an, with which We sent you, upon them, seeking from them in return something of the world."

The view that I hold to be most correct in this matter is the view of those who said: the meaning is: "And do not show favour to your Lord by regarding your righteous deed as great."

I say this is more correct because it occurs in the context of verses in which Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to strive in calling to Him and to be patient over the harm he suffers in doing so. Thus this verse is more fitting to be one of the kinds of those (commands) than to be of something else. It is reported on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud that in his recitation it was (wa la tamnun an tastakthir) [[Hadith 198. Badil, with a damma on the bā' and a fatḥa on the dāl: he is Ibn Maysara al-Uqayli, a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i). This report is connected by a sound chain, because 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq stated in it that "someone who heard the Prophet ﷺ" informed him, and the anonymity of a Companion does not harm, as is well known. Connecting the chain by mentioning an unnamed Companion is an addition from a trustworthy narrator, and so it is accepted.

Ibn Kathir (1: 54–55) mentioned this connected report, then pointed to the three mursal reports, then said: "In a report from 'Urwa there occurs the naming of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, and Allah knows best." However, he did not mention who transmitted the report from 'Urwa to which he refers. Then Ibn Kathir said: "Ibn Mardawayh has narrated, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, on the authority of Badil ibn Maysara, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: 'I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about "those who have earned anger," and he said: "The Jews." I said: "Those who have gone astray?" He said: "The Christians."' " The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in Fath al-Bari (8: 122) pointed to this report of Ibn Mardawayh from Abu Dharr "with a good chain." He also mentioned that the connected report of 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, "that someone who heard the Prophet ﷺ informed him," was narrated by Ahmad. These reports are also found in al-Suyuti (1: 16) and al-Shawkani (1: 14–15). The interpretation of (al-Dallin) will come with these chains at 210, 211, 212, 213. At 211 the identification of 'Urwa, who is in the chain at 197, will come.]]

And His words: ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾.

He, may He be exalted, says: "And for your Lord, be patient over what you encounter of hardship in it."

A group of the interpreters said something similar to what we have said, though there is some difference among the interpreters on this.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾, he said: "Over what you were given."
* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾, he said: "He bore a great task: fighting the Arabs, then the non-Arabs after the Arabs, for the sake of Allah."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: "And for your Lord, be patient over your giving."

Those who said this:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾, he said: "Be patient over your giving."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: "Be patient over your giving to Allah."
* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾, he said: "Your giving: be patient over it."

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿When the trumpet is sounded, (8) that Day will be a difficult Day, (9) not easy for the disbelievers. (10) Leave Me with the one whom I created alone, (11) and to whom I gave abundant wealth (12)﴾.

His, the Exalted's, saying, ﴿When the Trumpet is blown into﴾ (fa-idha nufikha fi al-sur), ﴿then that Day will be a difficult Day﴾, means: a severe day.

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of ta'wil (early Qur'anic exegetes and interpreters) have said.

Those who said this:

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl and Asbat related to us, from Mutarrif, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿When it is sounded in the Naqur, then that Day will be a difficult Day﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth, bowed his forehead, and is listening, waiting to be commanded to blow it?" The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And children present with him (13) And I made for him [wealth] well-spread (14) Then he desires that I should give more (15) No! Indeed, he has been stubborn toward Our verses (16) I will drive him to a steep ascent (17)﴾

.

Allah, may He be remembered, says: "And I made for him children present with him," and it is mentioned that they were ten.

Those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And children present with him﴾: he said, "He had ten sons."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And I made for him [wealth] well-spread﴾

Allah, may He be remembered, says: "And I extended for him his livelihood extensively."

As:

When he places his hand, it melts; when he lifts it, it returns; when he places his foot, likewise."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "As-su'ud is a mountain of fire, one climbs in it for seventy autumns, then falls back down, and so on forever."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding ﴿I will drive him to a steep ascent﴾: he said, "A hardship of punishment."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿I will drive him to a steep ascent﴾: i.e., punishment from which there is no relief.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatada regarding ﴿I will drive him to a steep ascent﴾: he said, "A hardship of punishment."

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿I will drive him to a steep ascent﴾: he said, "Exhaustion from punishment."

Qatadah said: "He came out of his mother's womb alone, so this verse was revealed up to nineteen."

He said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah entered upon Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah, may Allah be pleased with him, asking him about the Qur'an. *And indeed I was troubled by her aversion, which I saw,*
*And her turning away from my need, and her scowling* [[taqaddama ilayhi bi-shay': amarahu bi-fi'lihi aw ityanihi.]]

As for His saying: ﴿This is not but the word of a human being⁠﴾

He, may He be exalted, says, informing about the saying of the one called al-Walid concerning the Qur'an: ﴿This is not but the word of a human being⁠﴾: what this one whom Muhammad recites is nothing but the word of a human being. That is: it is nothing but the speech of a son of Adam, and it is not the speech of Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 74, verses 26–31:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿I will expose him to Saqar. And what can make you know what Saqar is? It leaves nothing and spares nothing. It scorches the human being. Over it are nineteen.﴾ ﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve—so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain and those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt, and so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it is not but a reminder to humanity.﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿I will expose him to Saqar﴾ means: I will cast him into one of the gates of Hell, named Saqar. Saqar is not declined (in the diptote form), because it is one of the names of Hell. ﴿And what can make you know what Saqar is?﴾ means: He, the Exalted, says: And what could make you know, O Muhammad, what Saqar is? Then Allah, the Exalted, explained what Saqar is, saying: It is a Fire ﴿that leaves nothing﴾ of those in it alive, and ﴿spares nothing﴾ of those in it dead; rather, it burns them every time their skins are renewed.

The people of interpretation said similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾: "It neither causes to die nor gives life."

- al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

- Muhammad ibn 'Ammara al-Asadi related to me, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, who said: Abu Layla informed us, from Murthid, regarding His saying: ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾: "It leaves none of them unconsumed by eating them; and when they are re-created for it, it does not leave them until it seizes them and eats them."

His saying: ﴿It scorches the human being﴾

He, the Exalted, means: it changes the complexion of its people. ﴿Lawwaha﴾ (scorcher) is a description of Saqar, and it is raised (as marfu') because it is a predicate ("it is a scorcher"), and it is indefinite while Saqar is definite, because of what it contains of the meaning of praise.

The people of interpretation said similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "The skin."

- Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, who said: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Razin, ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "It scorches the skin with a blast, and leaves it blacker than the night."

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam related to me, who said: my father related to us, and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Hilal, who said: Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "Their bodies are blackened by it."

- Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "That is, one that burns the skin."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "It says: it burns the human's skin."

- Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "It changes the complexion of humans, burns humans; it is said: 'His standing in the sun has blackened him.'" Then he said: "The Fire changes their colours."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu Razin, ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "It changed their skins and they turned black."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu Razin, similarly.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "That is, the human's complexion; it says: it burns his skin."

And it was related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this, that:

- 'Ali related to me, who said: Abu Salih related to us, who said: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "It says: 'mu'arridah' (exposing/presenting)." I fear that the report of 'Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn 'Abbas is an error, and that the place of "mu'arridah" should be "mughayyirah" (changing), but it was distorted in it.

His saying: ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Over Saqar are nineteen of the guardians.

It was mentioned that when this was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Jahl said:

- It was related to me by Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Over it are nineteen ...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and those who believe may increase in faith﴾. When Abu Jahl heard that, he said to the Quraysh: "May your mothers be bereaved! Does the son of Abu Kabsha inform you that the guardians of the Fire are nineteen while you are the multitude? Would not each ten of you be unable to overpower a single one of the guardians of Hell?" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was inspired to go to Abu Jahl, take him by the hand in the valley of Makkah, and say to him: ﴿Woe to you, and woe again! Then woe to you, and woe again!﴾ When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did this to him, Abu Jahl said: "By Allah, neither you nor your Lord can do anything!" So Allah disgraced him on the day of Badr.

- Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: "It was mentioned to us that when this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: 'O assembly of Quraysh, can each ten of you not overcome one of the guardians of the Fire, while you are the multitude?' [Note: it means God made this a practice from Him for all His creation to follow. He placed 'from Him for all His creation' earlier.] Your companion tells you that over it are nineteen."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: Abu Jahl said: "Muhammad informs you that the guardians of the Fire are nineteen, and you are the multitude, so that each ten gather against one."

- Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾: "Its guardians are nineteen."

His saying: ﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels﴾

He, the Exalted, says: We have not made the guardians of the Fire except angels, a reply to Abu Jahl's saying to the Quraysh: "Can each ten of you not overcome one of them? Who then can overcome the guardians of the Fire, who are the angels?"

The people of interpretation said similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd related to us, regarding His saying: ﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels﴾: "We did not make them men, so that each man would seize a man, as this one said."

His saying: ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾

He says: We have not made the number of these guardians except as a trial for those who disbelieved in Allah from the polytheists of Quraysh.

The people of interpretation said similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾: "Except as a tribulation."

Allah made the report about the number of the guardians of Hell a trial for those who disbelieved, because of their denial of it, and because some of them said to their companions: "I will suffice you against them."

The report concerning those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Nineteen﴾: "They made it a trial." Abu al-Ashudd ibn al-Jumahi said: "They will not reach my back (rtuti) until I repel them from Hell."

His saying: ﴿So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾

He, the Exalted, says: so that the People of the Torah and the Gospel may be certain of the truth of what is in their books of the report about the number of the guardians of Hell, since that agrees with what Allah revealed in His Book to Muhammad (ﷺ).

The people of interpretation said similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain, and those who believe may increase in faith﴾: "And indeed in the Torah and the Gospel it is nineteen. Allah willed that the People of the Book be certain, and that those who believe increase in faith."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾: "They find it written in their possession: the number of the guardians of the Fire."

- Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾: "The Qur'an confirms the books that were before it entirely, the Torah and the Gospel, that the guardians of the Fire are nineteen."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾: "That the People of the Book may be certain when the number of the guardians of the Fire agreed with what is in their books."

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾: "The number of the guardians of Hell is nineteen in the Torah and the Gospel."

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning this:

- Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾: "That you are the Messenger of Allah."

His saying: ﴿and those who believe may increase in faith﴾

He, the Exalted, says: and so that those who believed in Allah may increase in affirmation, in addition to their affirmation of Allah and His Messenger, by their affirming the number of the guardians of Hell.

His saying: ﴿and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt﴾

He says: the People of the Torah and the Gospel will not doubt the truth of that, nor the believers in Allah from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

His saying: ﴿and so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say﴾

He, the Exalted, says: and so that those in whose hearts is the disease of hypocrisy, and the disbelievers in Allah from the polytheists of Quraysh, will say: ﴿What did Allah intend by this as an example?﴾

As:

- Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿those in whose hearts is disease﴾: "That is, hypocrisy."

- Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾: "He says: so that He frightens us with these nineteen."

His saying: ﴿Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 74, verses 26–31:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿I will expose him to Saqar. And what can make you know what Saqar is? It leaves nothing and spares nothing. It scorches the human being. Over it are nineteen.﴾ ﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve—so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain and those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt, and so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it is not but a reminder to humanity.﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿I will expose him to Saqar﴾ means: I will cast him into one of the gates of Hell, named Saqar. Saqar is not declined (in the diptote form), because it is one of the names of Hell. ﴿And what can make you know what Saqar is?﴾ means: He, the Exalted, says: And what could make you know, O Muhammad, what Saqar is? Then Allah, the Exalted, explained what Saqar is, saying: It is a Fire ﴿that leaves nothing﴾ of those in it alive, and ﴿spares nothing﴾ of those in it dead; rather, it burns them every time their skins are renewed.

The people of interpretation said similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾: "It neither causes to die nor gives life."

- al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

- Muhammad ibn 'Ammara al-Asadi related to me, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, who said: Abu Layla informed us, from Murthid, regarding His saying: ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾: "It leaves none of them unconsumed by eating them; and when they are re-created for it, it does not leave them until it seizes them and eats them."

His saying: ﴿It scorches the human being﴾

He, the Exalted, means: it changes the complexion of its people. ﴿Lawwaha﴾ (scorcher) is a description of Saqar, and it is raised (as marfu') because it is a predicate ("it is a scorcher"), and it is indefinite while Saqar is definite, because of what it contains of the meaning of praise.

The people of interpretation said similar to what we have said on this.

- Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿scorcher to the human being﴾: "That is, one that burns the skin."

I fear that the report of 'Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn 'Abbas is an error, and that the place of "mu'arridah" should be "mughayyirah" (changing), but it was distorted in it.

His saying: ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Over Saqar are nineteen of the guardians.

It was mentioned that when this was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Jahl said:

- It was related to me by Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Over it are nineteen ...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and those who believe may increase in faith﴾. When Abu Jahl heard that, he said to the Quraysh: "May your mothers be bereaved! Does the son of Abu Kabsha inform you that the guardians of the Fire are nineteen while you are the multitude? So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was inspired to go to Abu Jahl, take him by the hand in the valley of Makkah, and say to him: ﴿Woe to you, and woe again! His saying: ﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels﴾

He, the Exalted, says: We have not made the guardians of the Fire except angels, a reply to Abu Jahl's saying to the Quraysh: "Can each ten of you not overcome one of them? Who then can overcome the guardians of the Fire, who are the angels?"

His saying: ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾

He says: We have not made the number of these guardians except as a trial for those who disbelieved in Allah from the polytheists of Quraysh.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 74, verses 32–37:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back, and by the morning when it brightens, indeed it is one of the greatest (calamities), a warning to mankind, to whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind.﴾

{Note: the verse being discussed is quoted in full above; the translation of its wording follows below.}

Here, may He be remembered, His saying ﴿Nay﴾ means: the matter is not as one says who claims that the guardians of Hell will suffice to overpower his polytheist companions so that they might repel them from it. Then our Lord, may He be exalted, swore, saying: ﴿By the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾, meaning: by the night when it turns away, departing.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said the like of what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ — when it turns away.

Others said something else:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ — its turning back: its darkening.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Basra read ﴿idh adbara﴾, and some of the reciters of Makkah and Kufa read ﴿idha dabara﴾.

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

The people of knowledge of the Arabic language differed on this. Some of the Kufans said: they are two dialects, one says dabara al-nahar and adbara, dabara al-sayf and adbara; he said: likewise qabila and aqbala. But when they say aqbala al-rakib and adbara, they say it only with the alif. Some of the Basrans said: ﴿wal-layli idha dabara﴾ means: when the day has turned back and was at its end; he said: it is said dabarani, meaning he came behind me, and adbara, meaning he turned away.

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that they are two dialects with one meaning, because it is related from the Arabs: "May God disfigure whatever is accepted from him and what turns back (dabara)." And secondly, the people of tafsir did not distinguish between the two readings in their explanations, which is evidence that they did so because they have one meaning.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾

He, may He be remembered, means: and by the morning when it shines.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾ — when it shines and comes. ﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest﴾ — He, may He be remembered, means: indeed Hell is one of the greatest, meaning: among the great matters.

Ahl al-ta'wil said the like of what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to me; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest﴾ — meaning: Hell.

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu Razin: ﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest﴾ — he said: Hell.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest﴾ — he said: this is the Fire.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest﴾ — he said: it is the Fire.

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest﴾ — meaning: Hell.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest﴾ — meaning Hell.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿A warning to mankind﴾

He, may He be remembered, means: indeed the Fire is one of the greatest, a warning to the children of Adam.

The people of ta'wil differed over the meaning of His saying ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, and what is described by it. Some of them said: by this is meant the Fire, and they said it is a qualifier of the pronoun in His saying ﴿indeed it (innaha)﴾, and they said: it is the warning. According to the view of these, ﴿warning﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial (qat') from ﴿one of the greatest﴾, since ﴿one of the greatest﴾ is definite and ﴿warning﴾ is indefinite, and the speech may be well concluded before it.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said: By God, mankind has not been warned of anything more calamitous than it, or of a calamity more calamitous than it.

Others said: rather, this is a description of God, may He be exalted, and it is a report from God about Himself that He is a warner to His creation. According to this view, the accusative of His saying ﴿warner﴾ must be taken as breaking off from the preceding sentence, so the meaning of the speech is: We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels, a warning to mankind, meaning: a warning to them; so His saying ﴿warner﴾ means a warning to them, as He said: ﴿So you will know how My warning was﴾, meaning My warning. It also means: indeed it is one of the greatest; We made that such a warner. So His saying ﴿indeed it is one of the greatest﴾ conveys the sense of "We made that so." This is what those who said it intended, God willing.

Those who said that:

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Razin: ﴿Indeed it is one of the greatest﴾ — he said: Hell. ﴿A warning to mankind﴾ — God says: I am a warner to you from it, so beware of it.

Others said: rather, this is a description of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and they said: ﴿warner﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial from what is in His saying "Arise (qum)", and they said: the meaning of the speech is: Arise as a warner to mankind and warn.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿a warning to mankind﴾: he said: the creation, the children of Adam, mankind. It was said to him: Muhammad is the warner? He said: Yes, he warns them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿To whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind﴾

He, may He be remembered, means: a warning to mankind, to whoever among you, O people, wills to advance in obedience to God, or to lag behind in disobedience to God.

Ahl al-ta'wil said the like of what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿To whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind﴾ — he said: whoever wills follows the obedience of God, and whoever wills lags behind from it.

Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿To whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind﴾ — to go forward in obedience to God, or to lag behind in His disobedience.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿A warning to mankind﴾

He, may He be remembered, means: indeed the Fire is one of the greatest, a warning to the children of Adam.

The people of ta'wil differed over the meaning of His saying ﴿a warning to mankind﴾, and what is described by it. Some of them said: by this is meant the Fire, and they said it is a qualifier of the pronoun in His saying ﴿indeed it (innaha)﴾, and they said: it is the warning. Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said: By God, mankind has not been warned of anything more calamitous than it, or of a calamity more calamitous than it.

According to this view, the accusative of His saying ﴿warner﴾ must be taken as breaking off from the preceding sentence, so the meaning of the speech is: We did not make the companions of the Fire except angels, a warning to mankind, meaning: a warning to them; so His saying ﴿warner﴾ means a warning to them, as He said: ﴿So you will know how My warning was﴾, meaning My warning. Ahl al-ta'wil said the like of what we have said on this.
