Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 74, verses 32–37:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it turns back, and by the morning when it brightens, indeed it is one of the greatest (calamities), a warning to mankind, to whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind.﴾

{Note: the verse being discussed is quoted in full above; the translation of its wording follows below.}

Here, may He be remembered, His saying ﴿Nay﴾ means: the matter is not as one says who claims that the guardians of Hell will suffice to overpower his polytheist companions so that they might repel them from it. Then our Lord, may He be exalted, swore, saying: ﴿By the moon, and by the night when it turns back﴾, meaning: by the night when it turns away, departing.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said the like of what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ — when it turns away.

Others said something else:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and by the night when it turns back﴾ — its turning back: its darkening.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Basra read ﴿idh adbara﴾, and some of the reciters of Makkah and Kufa read ﴿idha dabara﴾.

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

The people of knowledge of the Arabic language differed on this. Some of the Kufans said: they are two dialects, one says dabara al-nahar and adbara, dabara al-sayf and adbara; he said: likewise qabila and aqbala. But when they say aqbala al-rakib and adbara, they say it only with the alif. Some of the Basrans said: ﴿wal-layli idha dabara﴾ means: when the day has turned back and was at its end; he said: it is said dabarani, meaning he came behind me, and adbara, meaning he turned away.

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that they are two dialects with one meaning, because it is related from the Arabs: "May God disfigure whatever is accepted from him and what turns back (dabara)." And secondly, the people of tafsir did not distinguish between the two readings in their explanations, which is evidence that they did so because they have one meaning.

He, may He be remembered, means: and by the morning when it shines.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 74, verses 38–45:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, (38) except the companions of the right, (39) in gardens, they will ask one another, (40) about the criminals, (41) "What has brought you into Saqar?" (42) They will say, "We were not of those who prayed, (43) and we did not feed the needy, (44) and we used to engage in vain talk with those who engaged in vain talk." (45)﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: every soul, commanded and forbidden, is held in pledge in Hell for what it did of disobedience to God in the world, ﴿except the companions of the right﴾, for they are not held in pledge, but they are ﴿in gardens, they will ask one another about the criminals﴾.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾, he said: taken to account for its deeds.

* Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right﴾, he said: all people are locked up except the companions of the right.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right﴾, he said: they will not be called to account.

* Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God's words: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right﴾: the companions of the right are not held in pledge for their sins, but God forgives them, and he recited God's words: ﴿except the sincere servants of God﴾, he said: God does not take them to task for their evil deeds, but God forgives them and overlooks them, as He promised them.

* It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾, he said: every soul for which the word of punishment has preceded will be held in pledge by God in the Fire; God does not hold any of the people of Paradise in pledge. * Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿except the companions of the right﴾, he said: if one of them had the word of punishment preceding for him, his place would be made in the Fire where he would be held in pledge; but none of the people of Paradise is held in pledge; they are in gardens, asking one another.

The exegetes differed concerning the companions of the right mentioned by God in this place. Some of them said: they are the children of the Muslims.

Those who said so:

* Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, who said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from al-A'mash, from Uthman, from Zadhan, from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding this verse: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right﴾, he said: they are the young children.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, who said: Mu'ammal related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from Uthman Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan Abu 'Umar, from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding His words: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right﴾, he said: the children of the Muslims.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Uthman ibn 'Umayr Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan Abu 'Umar, from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, ﴿except the companions of the right﴾, he said: the children of the Muslims.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Yaqzan, from Zadhan, from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, ﴿except the companions of the right﴾, he said: they are the young children.

Others said: they are the angels.

Those who said so:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Waki' related to us, from Shurayk, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they are the angels. Those who said that the companions of the right in this place are the young children and the children of the Muslims said so because these had no sins, and they said: they would not ask the criminals ﴿What has brought you into Saqar?﴾ unless they had not committed sins in the world; and had they committed and known them, they would not have asked them what brought them into Saqar, because everyone among the children of Adam who reaches the limit of legal responsibility and is bound by the obligation of commanding and forbidding knows that no one is punished except for disobedience.

**The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:** ﴿So the intercession of the interceders will not benefit them﴾ [74:48] **﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the Reminder﴾** [74:49]

.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And we used to deny the Day of Judgment﴾

He, the Exalted, says: They said, "We used to deny the Day of Recompense, the Requital, the reward and the punishment, and we did not affirm any reward, punishment or reckoning." ﴿Until the Certainty came to us﴾, meaning: they said, "Until death, which is certain, came to us." ﴿So the intercession of the interceders will not benefit them﴾, meaning: those whom God permitted to intercede for the people of sins from among the people of tawhid (monotheism) will not intercede for them, so their intercession would not benefit them. In this verse there is clear evidence that God, the Exalted and Mighty, permits some of His creation to intercede for others.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Abu al-Zu'ara' narrated to us, from Abdullah, in a narration he mentioned concerning intercession, who said: "Then the angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous and the believers will intercede, and God will grant them intercession, and He will say: 'I am the Most Merciful of the merciful.' So He will bring out from the Fire more than what He brought out from all of creation from the Fire. Then He will say: 'I am the Most Merciful of the merciful.'" Then Abdullah recited: ﴿What led you into Saqar? They will say: We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the needy, and we used to plunge with the plungers, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment﴾, and he counted four with his hand, then said: "Do you see any good in these people? Lo, no one who has any good in him is left in it."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my uncle and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Zu'ara', who said: Abdullah said: "None will remain in the Fire except four, or the possessor of four." The doubt is from Abu Ja'far al-Tabari. Then he recited: ﴿What led you into Saqar? They will say: We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the needy, and we used to plunge with the plungers, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment﴾.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So the intercession of the interceders will not benefit them﴾: "You should know that God intercedes for the believers on the Day of Resurrection. It has been mentioned to us that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: 'Among my community there is a man through whose intercession God will admit into Paradise more than the Banu Tamim.'"

Al-Hasan said: "More than Rabi'ah and Mudar. We used to be told that the martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So the intercession of the interceders will not benefit them﴾, who said: "You should know that God intercedes for some of them on behalf of others."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 74, verses 50–53:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As if they were startled donkeys (50) fleeing from a lion (qaswarah) (51). Nay, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out (52). Nay! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter (53).﴾

Almighty God says: What is the matter with these polytheists, that they turn away from the Reminder, fleeing from it as startled donkeys flee ﴿from a lion﴾.

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying ﴿mustanfirah﴾ (startled). The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it with a kasra on the fa', and in the reading of some Meccans also, meaning "fleeing" (nafirah) [[In the printed edition: "in the opening..." and the pronoun in "fabihi" refers to "what He disciplined him with."]].

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is that both are well-known readings, sound in meaning, and whichever one the reciter reads is correct. Al-Farra' used to say: the fath and the kasr in this are both common in the speech of the Arabs; and he recited:

Hold back your donkey, for it is startled
in pursuit of she-asses who have run off to the open land.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿fled from a lion﴾: he said: qaswarat al-nabl (the lion of the arrows).

Others said: they are the hunters.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: meaning, the men of the hunt.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding this verse ﴿fled from a lion﴾: he said: they are the hunters.

- Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: they are the hunters.

Others said: they are the groups of men.

Those who said this:

- Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us; and Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about al-qaswarah, and he said: I do not know of anyone among the Arabs who knows its language better: the lion; it is the gathering of men.

- Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told us, saying: I do not know of anyone among the Arabs who knows its language better: the lion, it is the gathering of men.

- Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told us, saying: I heard my father narrate, saying: Dawud told us, saying: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of the Banu Hashim, told me, saying: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about al-qaswarah, and he said: the gathering of men. Have you not heard what such-and-such a woman said in the Jahiliyyah:

O daughter of Luay, best of the best,
her affairs in the tribe are like the qaswarah.

[[Its meaning: that is, what concerns her and what she intends.]]

Others said: it is the voices of men.

Those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah told us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: he said: the people's voices (rikz).

Abu Kurayb said: Sufyan said: ﴿Do you perceive any of them, or hear from them a whisper (rikzan)?﴾

Others said: rather, it is the lion.

Those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Hurayrah, ﴿fled from a lion﴾: he said: it is the lion.

- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn Sayлан, that Abu Hurayrah used to say regarding the saying of God ﴿fled from a lion﴾: he said: it is the lion.

- Muhammad ibn Ma'mar told me, saying: Hisham told us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding the saying of God ﴿fled from a lion﴾: the lion.

- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Qays informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding the saying of God ﴿fled from a lion﴾: he said: it is the lion.

- Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Khidash told me, saying: Salm ibn Qutaybah told me, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he was asked about His saying ﴿fled from a lion﴾: he said: in Arabic it is the lion, in Persian: shar, in Nabataean: aryā, in Abyssinian: qaswarah.

- 'Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying ﴿fled from a lion﴾: he says: the lion.

- Abu al-Sa'ib told me, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath told us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: the lion.

- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿fled from a lion﴾: the qaswarah: the lion.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Nay, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out﴾

Almighty God says: the state of these polytheists in turning away from this Qur'an is not that they do not know it is from God; rather, each man among them wants to be given a book sent down to him from heaven.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Nay, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out﴾: some people said: O Muhammad, if it pleases you that we follow you, bring us a book addressed specifically to so-and-so and so-and-so, in which we are commanded to follow you. Qatadah said: they want to be given a quittance without works.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Nay, each one of them wants to be given scrolls spread out﴾: to so-and-so from the Lord of the worlds.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Nay! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾

Almighty God says: the matter is not as they claim, that if they were given scrolls spread out they would believe. ﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾: that is, but they do not fear God's punishment, nor do they believe in the Resurrection, the reward and the punishment; and that is what prompted them to turn away from the Reminder of God, and made it easy for them to abandon listening to His revelation and His sending down.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Nay! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾: what corrupted them is that they did not believe in the Hereafter nor fear it; that is what corrupted them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 74, verses 54–56:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, verily it is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember unless Allah wills. He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness.﴾

His saying, may His praise be exalted, "Nay, verily it is a reminder" means: The matter is not as these polytheists say about this Qur'an, that it is sorcery that has an effect, or that it is the speech of a human being. Rather, it is a reminder from Allah to His creation, by which He reminds them.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this. 

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "Nay, verily it is a reminder," that is: the Qur'an.

* * *

As for His saying, "So whoever wills may remember it,"

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Whoever among the servants of Allah whom Allah has reminded through this Qur'an wills to remember it, takes admonition and acts upon what it contains of Allah's commands and prohibitions. "And they will not remember unless Allah wills" means: they will not remember this Qur'an so as to be admonished by it and act upon what it contains, unless Allah wills that they remember it; for no one has power over anything except that Allah wills to empower him over it and grants him the ability to do it.

* * *

As for His saying, "He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness,"

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Allah is worthy that His servants fear His punishment for their disobedience to Him, so that they avoid His disobedience and hasten to His obedience. "And worthy of forgiveness" means: He is worthy to forgive their sins when they do that, and not to punish them for them when they repent from them.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness," he said: Our Lord deserves that His prohibitions be feared, and He is worthy of forgiveness, forgiving sins.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness," he said: Worthy that His prohibitions be feared, and "worthy of forgiveness": worthy to forgive sins.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Muddaththir.
